configuration.limitation: Employees Provident Fund Act 1991, s.43 and the Third Schedule — Part A (Malaysian citizens, permanent residents and pre-1-August-1998 electors below the age of 60) and Part E (Malaysian citizens aged 60 and above). The first printed row of both Parts is NIL: wages of RM0.01 to RM10.00 attract no contribution, which is the zero band below. A non-citizen contributes under Part F instead, which is the separate EPF_NON_CITIZEN scheme below; an employment belongs to exactly one of the EPF schemes, decided by its employment_statutory_facts registration. A permanent resident or pre-1998 elector who has attained 60 contributes under Part C, which is the separate EPF_PR scheme — the 60-and-above ladder here is Part E and by its own terms reaches Malaysian citizens only, which is what the eligibility predicate says. Contribution ceases at the age of 75 (KWSP, Employer Mandatory Contribution, note 1: https://www.kwsp.gov.my/en/employer/responsibilities/mandatory-contribution), which is the zero terminal band. EPF Act 1991 First Schedule para (13): a person who has attained seventy-five is not an employee for the Act, and s.51(2B)(a) credits nothing to a member after seventy-five — so no part of the Third Schedule, F included, is charged from the month the person turns 75 (`age < 75` on every rung). Act A1760 (2025) prints no age in Part F because the exclusion sits in the First Schedule. Third Schedule Parts A, C, E and F: above the table the total contribution is rounded up to the next ringgit and the employer’s share is that total less the employee’s rounded share, never two separate round-ups. EPF Act s.2 “wages” excludes a retrenchment, lay-off or termination benefit and a payment in lieu of notice (TERMINATION_BENEFIT, NOTICE_IN_LIEU outside the base). Third Schedule Part A note under the RM5,000 row — "Where the employer pays bonus to an employee who receives monthly wages of RM5,000.00 and below, and upon receiving the said bonus renders the wages received for that month to exceed RM5,000.00, the employer’s contribution shall be calculated at the rate of 13% of the amount of wages for the month. The total contribution which includes cents shall be rounded to the next ringgit." The first rule prices that month: `ordinary` (the month’s wages without additional remuneration) at or below RM5,000 and the whole base above it; the employee’s share stays on the printed row (11% of the band’s upper limit, or of the wage above RM20,000) and the employer’s is the rounded total less it (KWSP, Third Schedule effective 1 October 2025, Part A p.12: https://www.kwsp.gov.my/documents/d/guest/third_schedule_from_-1-october-2025). a non-citizen who became a member before 1 August 1998 stays on Part A below 60 (and Part C from 60, EPF_PR) rather than Part F — the EPF election `member_before_1998` (Act A1760; KWSP, Contribution for Non-Malaysian Citizen Employees: https://www.kwsp.gov.my/en/employer/responsibilities/non-malaysian-citizen-employees). Employment Act 1955 s.60A(3)(b) (AGC reprint as at 1 August 2023) makes overtime only the hours beyond the normal hours of work, and s.60A(4) proviso says holiday work "shall not be construed as overtime work"; the s.60D(3)(a)(i) two days' wages for work within the normal hours on a paid holiday settle on their own line (`bands[].line`, read as `DAY_PAY`), not OVERTIME. KWSP Employer FAQ 21: wages for work on a holiday are EPF wages "unless the work attendance is considered as overtime", so `DAY_PAY` enters the EPF wage. rest-day work within the normal hours (Employment Act 1955 s.60(3)(a)/(b)) settles on REST_DAY_WORK (`DAY_PAY`), which is EPF wages (EPF Act 1991 s.2 excludes only "overtime payment"). Only s.60(3)(c) hours beyond the normal hours are overtime (s.60A(3)). the Third Schedule bonus exception compares the whole contribution wage less BONUS, including encashment, back pay and other non-bonus additional wages. It requires a positive BONUS; the remuneration classification used to project tax relief does not redefine the statutory bonus exception. Unchanged law transcribed in place. The same Part A/C bonus note covers pre-1-August-1998 non-citizen electors: Part A para 1(c) and Part C para 1(c); eligibility matches the ordinary printed ladder. CEL charges Part A on the printed band upper limit (RM20 bands to RM5,000, RM100 bands to RM20,000; employer 13% to RM5,000 or where only additional wages lift the month over it, 12% above), each share rounded up to the ringgit; above RM20,000 the percentage of the wage with the employer the rounded total less the employee; Part E is the employer 4% alone. PR years one and two are not applied on this engine context.

Contributions stop at 75 (KWSP, Contribution for Non-Malaysian Citizen Employees: liable below 75 years of age). EPF Act 1991 First Schedule para (13): a person who has attained seventy-five is not an employee for the Act, and s.51(2B)(a) credits nothing to a member after seventy-five — so no part of the Third Schedule, F included, is charged from the month the person turns 75 (`age < 75` on every rung). Pre-1 August 1998 non-citizen members remain on Parts A/C through the member_before_1998 election. The two 2% shares are therefore totalled and the total is rounded up to the ringgit once. Part F does not say which share carries the rounding. KWSP’s non-Malaysian employee FAQ (https://www.kwsp.gov.my/en/employer/responsibilities/non-malaysian-citizen-employees) rounds each share up (RM36 + RM36 = RM72); the Act governs, and the per-share convention of 2026-09-25 is withdrawn. Employment Act 1955 s.60A(3)(b) (AGC reprint as at 1 August 2023) makes overtime only the hours beyond the normal hours of work, and s.60A(4) proviso says holiday work "shall not be construed as overtime work"; the s.60D(3)(a)(i) two days' wages for work within the normal hours on a paid holiday settle on their own line (`bands[].line`, read as `DAY_PAY`), not OVERTIME. KWSP Employer FAQ 21: wages for work on a holiday are EPF wages "unless the work attendance is considered as overtime", so `DAY_PAY` enters the EPF wage. rest-day work within the normal hours (Employment Act 1955 s.60(3)(a)/(b)) settles on REST_DAY_WORK (`DAY_PAY`), which is EPF wages (EPF Act 1991 s.2 excludes only "overtime payment"). Only s.60(3)(c) hours beyond the normal hours are overtime (s.60A(3)). Rates moved 2026-10-01 to the version's EPF_PART_F table (reference_rows): the band above RM0.00 carries the 2% employee and 2% employer shares; the rule keeps the rounding (employee share to the cent down, total up to the next ringgit, employer = total less employee).

configuration.limitation: What the CEL computes (2026-10-06, pass 3): a resident (citizen or permanent resident, or the PCB standing’s election tax_residency RESIDENT) is charged the LHDN MTD Specification 2026 D year-to-date formula — P = Σ(Y − K*) + (Y1 − K1) + (Y2 − K2)n + (Yt − Kt) − (D + S + DU + SU + QC), with Σ(Y) the earlier months’ PCB remuneration (`year` parts), K* the EPF employee shares charged earlier in the year (`charged.year.EPF*`), K1 the month’s EPF share on the EPF-wage part, Y2 = Y1, K2 = min(K1, [4,000 − K* − K1] ÷ n), n the months left in the year, all EPF relief within RM4,000; D RM9,000, S RM4,000 for a spouse without income (employee.marital_status MARRIED and spouse_status WITHOUT_INCOME), DU RM7,000 (employee.disabled), SU a further RM6,000 (election spouse_disabled), QC the declared child-relief counts (elections children_*: RM2,000 under 18 or studying, RM8,000 tertiary or disabled, RM16,000 disabled in tertiary education, half amounts for a shared child); Schedule 1 rates; the s.6A(2)(a) RM400 rebate and the s.6A(2)(b) RM400 spouse rebate when P ≤ RM35,000. Normal MTD = [tax − (Z + X)] ÷ (n + 1), X the MTD charged earlier in the year (`charged.year.PCB`) and Z the earlier months’ payroll zakat (the standing’s zakat_monthly × earlier months), truncated to the sen and rounded up to 5 sen; additional remuneration (`additional`, `additional_non_epf`) adds the year’s tax with Yt − Kt less Z + X and n + 1 normal MTDs, rounded the same way; each component under RM10 is not deducted; the month’s payroll zakat is then rebated. Parts `non_epf` / `additional_non_epf` are PCB remuneration that is not EPF wages (overtime, travel, notice pay), so K is not taken on them. Category caps, medical and education sublimits, shared contribution limits, alimony/spouse limits, claim intervals and joint-home interest shares apply to the tax-year totals. Corrections retain a separate reference. Voluntary EPF allocations under the RM4,000 and RM3,000 limits must not overlap. SOCSO/EIS (and SKBBK) contributions are relieved only as claimed on Form TP1 item C14 (ITA 1967 s.46(1)(n); MTD Specification 2026 D.2(ii) "Optional deductions" item k, RM350 a year): payroll contributions are never relieved automatically — the only automatic relief is the individual RM9,000 (D.2(i) item a), and the specification's own worked examples carry LP1 = 0 on a RM5,500 wage. Housing declarations establish first-home eligibility and supply the purchase price, sale agreement date, first interest year and qualifying interest paid by all owners.

LHDN D(2), Steps 1(C/E) and 4: normal MTD is truncated to cents and rounded up to five cents before annualisation. Additional MTD uses that projected amount and accumulated PCB and zakat.

Sources: https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-2026.pdf ; https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/bm-borang-tp1-2026.pdf ; https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/nota-penerangan-tp1-2026.pdf

Projected EPF relief uses the contribution on normal remuneration for future months. Current additional-remuneration EPF is included once in the additional-pay calculation and excluded from the normal-pay calculation, following LHDN D(b) and E(13).

Voluntary EPF under TP1 C11(a) shares the RM4,000 statutory cap with compulsory contributions. Normal and additional remuneration each apply that cap using their own projected compulsory-contribution relief; the additional-pay base cannot reduce normal-pay relief. TP1 C11(b) remains a separate RM3,000 allocation.

TP1 D1 external zakat and qualifying religious-travel departure levy are rebates in the accepted claim month, not remuneration deductions. Full rebate amounts remain in statutory history even when current PCB is zero (LHDN E(5), E(15)). Prior-employer amounts use the opening rebate balance. The levy is limited to two lifetime journeys; dated claim and correction records share a journey reference, and the required prior-year count includes claims through other employers.

LHDN 2026 D(3)-(5) approved REP, knowledge-worker and relocation C-suite profiles calculate 15% of projected chargeable income after relief and accumulated PCB/rebates, not 15% of gross pay. Additional remuneration enters the annual projection once. REP and knowledge-worker profiles retain the RM400/RM800 low-chargeable-income rebate; C-suite has no such rebate. Typed declarations require approval reference and covered assessment years. Resident status remains separate. REP requires Malaysian citizenship; C-suite requires non-citizenship. Approval eligibility, qualifying employer and current Ministerial conditions require the referenced evidence. REP and relocation C-suite periods are exactly five consecutive assessment years.

Relocation C-suite minimum basic salary: RM25,000 monthly, P.U. (A) 242/2023 rule 5(d). Five consecutive years: rule 7. Gazette mirror: https://www.maicsa.org.my/media/8567/technical_announcements_230817_1_3.pdf . Formal incentive approvals and conditions remain distinct from the MTD amount formula.

Approval controls: P.U. (A) 151/2012 rules 2-5 as amended and LHDN Public Ruling 1/2026 require an approved resident Malaysian REP individual and five consecutive assessment years. P.U. (A) 344/2010 rules 2, 4-7 require Ministerial approval through IRDA and current employment in a qualifying activity with a designated company while residing in the specified region. P.U. (A) 242/2023 rules 3-7 require a non-citizen resident in a C-suite position with the approved company, the conditions in the Minister's approval letter, RM25,000 minimum monthly basic salary, and exactly five consecutive assessment years.

 LHDN MTD Specification 2026 D(a) note (p.9) — "With effect from August 2017, MTD for resident on foreign workers is applicable to employees with an employment contract of or more than 182 days": a FOREIGNER whose fixed-term contract runs 182 days or more (`person.employment.contract_days`, first day to last inclusive) is withheld at resident MTD whatever the recorded tax residency. Owner rule 2026-09-28: law silent on an open-ended contract (contract_days 0) — the recorded tax residency governs, D(a)'s 30% for one not known to be resident; lawful because the note names a stated contract length and the employer may record RESIDENT. A PERMANENT_RESIDENT is not a foreign worker (no VP(TE)) and keeps the recorded status.

 ITA 1967 Schedule 6 para 25C (AGC online text as at 1 January 2026) and LHDN MTD Specification 2026 E(9) item v (p.21): a long service award is exempt up to RM2,000 per employee per year of assessment only where the employee has exercised employment for more than ten years with the same employer (`service_months_exact > 120`); the exempt part leaves the MTD base (D(a): exempt income is excluded from MTD remuneration), the excess is additional remuneration.

 ITA 1967 s.7(1)(a)-(c), (1A) and Schedule 6 paras 21-22 (AGC online text as at 1 January 2026) read the days an individual is in Malaysia. Where the employee's stays are recorded (`presence_periods`, an entry or exit day a whole day, counted through the period end), the recorded days decide: 182 or more days in the basis year (s.7(1)(a)), a stay unbroken from 182 or more consecutive days in the previous basis year (s.7(1)(b)), or 90 or more days with 90 or more in three of the four preceding basis years (s.7(1)(c)(ii)) withholds resident MTD whatever the recorded tax residency; a non-resident with 60 days or fewer in the basis year is exempt under para 21(a), and past 60 days (para 22(a)) the months already exempt this year are recovered at 30% on the para 22 recovery default, then 30% a month. Without recorded stays the declared residency and the `pcb_sch6_para21` / `pcb_sch6_para22_recover` elections govern as before. Not read from the ledger: s.7(1)(b) temporary absences (record the absence inside the stay only where the proviso treats it as presence), s.7(1)(c)(i) residence by (b) or (d) in a preceding year with under 90 days, and s.7(1)(d) (the following year is not known at payroll) - the recorded tax residency still covers these. Income Tax Act 1967 Schedule 6 paragraph 21 applies to employment exercised while in Malaysia for no more than 60 days, not physical presence days alone (LHDN Public Ruling 2/2026, https://www.hasil.gov.my/media/ikelbhz0/pr-2-2026-tax-treatment-of-foreign-nationals-exercising-employment-in-malaysia.pdf). Until dated in-Malaysia employment exercise is recorded, an apparent paragraph 21 election refuses; ordinary residence rules and non-resident withholding continue. Employment Act 1955 s.60A(3)(b) (AGC reprint as at 1 August 2023) makes overtime only the hours beyond the normal hours of work, and s.60A(4) proviso says holiday work "shall not be construed as overtime work"; the s.60D(3)(a)(i) two days' wages for work within the normal hours on a paid holiday settle on their own line (`bands[].line`, read as `DAY_PAY`), not OVERTIME. Encoded 2026-10-07 (round 6): TP1 deductions declared for the month (election tp1_monthly_deductions, LP1) are taken for every month of the year so far, ΣLP + LP1; a mid-year joiner's previous employer figures (TP3: tp3_prior_remuneration, tp3_prior_epf, tp3_prior_mtd) join Σ(Y − K) and X; an approved REP or knowledge-worker employee is taxed at 15% of chargeable income less the RM400 self and spouse rebates at RM35,000 or below, and an approved non-citizen C-suite employee at 15% with no rebate, within the approval years (elections pcb_tax_profile, pcb_approval_first_year, pcb_approval_last_year; MTD Specification 2026 sections 3–5, https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-2026.pdf). A CP38 instalment is its own ad hoc class (CP38_INSTALMENT), so it never enters X. Above RM20,000 and for Part F the EPF relief K follows the statutory exact shares.

name: Human Resource Development Levy (HRD Corp)

configuration.limitation: Pembangunan Sumber Manusia Berhad Act 2001, s.14 and the First Schedule, as expanded to all industries from 1 March 2021. Registration is COMPULSORY at 10 or more Malaysian employees and the levy is 1% of monthly wages; at 5 to 9 Malaysian employees registration is OPTIONAL and the 0.5% levy falls due only once the employer has elected to register (HRD Corp, Registered Employers). the headcount test counts Malaysian employees alone (`company.headcount_citizens`), as the levy base already did; the 5-to-9 election is a NOT_REGISTERED fact on this scheme. PSMB Act 2001 s.2: the levy and the headcount test are on Malaysian citizens (`citizenship == "CITIZEN"`); a permanent resident is not a Malaysian employee. HRD correction 2026-09-25: Act 612 ss.2, 14–15 and Employers Circular 19/2010 exclude domestic servants and part-time wages; the mandatory employer levy remains due without registration while the optional class needs an election. HRD employer-class correction 2026-09-25: Act 612 ss.1, 2, 13–16, P.U.(A) 84/2021 First Schedule and HRD Corp Employers Circular 5/2018. Employer-declared Form 2 Malaysian employee count and dated employer standing select the rate. P.U. (A) 13/2026 exempts registered employers in its listed education MSIC industries for the 2026 levy-contribution period. HRD base correction 2026-09-28 (transcription, every version): Act 612 s.2 “wages” (AGC reprint 2017) “includes any leave pay”, and HRD Corp’s Levy Calculation Guideline repeats “includes any leave pay and arrears of wages”; neither lists payment for untaken leave among the exclusions (a)–(f) or the exempted pay elements, and it is not the (d) gratuity on discharge, so s.60E(3A) payment for untaken annual leave is levy wages. Employer 1% HRD levy on citizen wages. PART_I headcount and registration class live on the entity; this CEL does not re-test Form 2 counts.
